title: robots.txt exists and parses
question: Can an agent fetch /robots.txt and parse it?
method: GET /robots.txt. Pass on a 200 text response that parses under RFC 9309; warn on 404 (everything allowed by default, but intent is unstated); fail on 5xx, a challenge page or unparseable content.

title: Sitemap declared and reachable
question: Is there a sitemap an agent can fetch?
method: Collect Sitemap: lines from robots.txt, then try /sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml and /wp-sitemap.xml. Pass when one returns parseable XML with at least one URL or child sitemap.

title: Product URLs in sitemap
question: Does the sitemap list product pages?
method: Pass when the sitemap index contains a product sitemap (WooCommerce: product-sitemap.xml or wp-sitemap-posts-product-*.xml) or the URL set contains URLs matching product path patterns.

title: Link response headers
question: Does the site point agents at its machine-readable resources through Link headers?
method: Read the Link response headers of the home page and one sampled product page. Pass when any relation an agent can use is present: llms-txt, alternate with type text/markdown, api-catalog, service-desc, describedby, license with type application/rsl+xml, or ucp (the relation Shopify sends on every response). Fail when none is. Low weight: a convention, not a requirement.

title: llms.txt is valid when present
question: If the site publishes llms.txt, is it a usable file?
method: GET /llms.txt. A 404 or 410 skips the check as not applicable: the file is optional and no major assistant documents reading it, so its absence is never scored. On a 200 the body must be text, not HTML (a soft 404 fails), and must start with an H1, the only element the proposal requires; warn when it has no links; pass otherwise. The same rule Lighthouse applies.

title: llms.txt links to the catalog
question: Does llms.txt lead an agent to the catalog as data?
method: When llms.txt is present and valid, pass when one of its links points at a product feed, a product API, a product sitemap or the shop index. Fail when it links only to prose pages. Skipped when there is no llms.txt.

title: Sitemap lastmod is present and plausible
question: Can an agent tell from the sitemap what changed and when?
method: Read <lastmod> in the sitemaps fetched. Pass when at least 80 percent of entries carry a valid W3C datetime and the values differ from one another; warn when fewer entries carry one, or when every value is identical (a timestamp generated at request time, which crawlers learn to ignore); fail when none carry one. Bing names lastmod a key signal for how fast changes reach its AI answers; Google uses it when it is consistently accurate.

title: Listing pages link to products and further pages
question: Can a crawler walk from a category page to every product and to the next page with plain links?
method: GET the sampled listing page (a shop, collection or category page linked from the home page). Count same-origin anchors to product URLs and look for crawlable pagination: a rel=next link, or anchors whose URL names a page number (/page/2/, ?page=2, ?p=2, ?paged=2). Pass when the page links to products and either paginates with links or shows no pagination at all. Warn when products are listed but the only way to more of them is a button or infinite scroll (Google's crawlers do not click or scroll, and Bing asks for standard anchor links), or when no product link is found in the HTML. Not applicable when no listing page was found.
